findings.claim: Signed favorable-versus-comparison endpoint contrasts at the observed selection nodes are strongest and most reproducible for the short-range pair-distance shells: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the branch-adjusted raw and adjusted covariance/correlation rows for these kernels. These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a radial shell-density observable, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not an interaction energy.

Shape components carry signed endpoint contrasts, with shape_yy the most consistent (integrated z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and shape_xx (q 8.1e-4) and shape_yz (q 0.035) also negative; shape_zz is negative but weaker (q 0.067). The regional local_cyy enrichment_z is negative at every landmark (all 20 regions, q at or below 0.0166), so the shape_yy signal is not confined to one region. These are coordinate-moment contrasts, not evidence of a chemical mechanism.

Landmark softmin and occupancy contrasts are mixed in sign across regions rather than globally coherent: landmark_00_softmin is negative (q 8.1e-4) while landmark_00_occupancy3 is positive (q 2.4e-4); landmark_02_softmin, landmark_03_softmin, landmark_05_softmin, landmark_06_softmin, landmark_12_softmin, landmark_15_softmin and landmark_18_softmin are positive, whereas landmark_04_softmin, landmark_10_softmin, landmark_14_occupancy5, landmark_15_occupancy5, landmark_16_occupancy5 and landmark_18_occupancy5 are negative. The regional soft_mass enrichment_z is positive at landmarks 00, 07, 10 and 17 and negative at landmarks 11 and 12. Because softmin is a normalized soft minimum distance and occupancy is a radial shell density, a sign on one observable cannot be read as a shared quality axis.

Global pose descriptors are weak or null: global_centroid_y has a small negative endpoint contrast (q 0.014) and global_centroid_x and global_centroid_z are not distinguishable from zero (q 0.257 and 0.481). In the branch-adjusted adjusted_covariance and adjusted_correlation strata the centroid rows are likewise null (e.g. global_centroid_x q 0.965, global_centroid_y q 0.864, global_centroid_z q 0.913). Centroid displacement is therefore not a supported direction on this evidence.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible negative signals in the branch-adjusted table: joint_innovation_RMS_A (raw covariance q 0.038, adjusted covariance q 0.020, raw correlation q 9.3e-5, adjusted correlation q 2.8e-4), joint_internal_RMS_A (q 0.044, 0.030, 1.5e-4, 9.7e-4) and joint_translation_RMS_A (q 0.095, 0.072, 0.087, 0.052) all have negative whole-window means with same-sign batch fractions of 0.71 to 1.0. These are joint-motion residual diagnostics, not rigid-motion residuals of the region moments themselves and not atom velocities.

Within-selector joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment (0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with teacher innovation-contrast alignment (0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), but negatively associated with observed child score gain (-0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). Teacher contrast is predominantly internal (internal fraction 0.787) with smaller translation (0.132) and rotation (0.081) fractions, and teacher sign calibration cosine is high (0.973). These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal selection effects.

The information audit reports that the compressed-choice excess over fixed-frame RMS is 0.081 A (bootstrap CI 0.070-0.092) and that compressed chosen teacher score correlation is 0.102 (CI 0.065-0.140) versus full chosen teacher score correlation 0.064 (CI 0.021-0.103); top-4 teacher overlap is 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515). The audit itself states this is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction, not a causal affinity effect. The curve_support audit additionally records that no selected curve has legendre_runtime_allowed true, with relative node RMSE 0.386-0.931 and 0-15 strong sign-conflict nodes per curve.

The observed-node linear fits for landmark_00 and landmark_01 features show large first-rate and last-rate z values of opposite sign (for example landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z -72.4 versus last_rate_z 5.5; landmark_01_local_dz -58.5 versus 8.8) with 3-10 sign changes and 1-18 strong sign conflicts per feature, and polynomial_accepted is false for every row. The continuous_functions registry states these are observed values_z at shared times interpolated within observed support only, with extrapolation_allowed false, so the fitted rates are not a trajectory velocity force and do not establish a monotone trend.

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity: lineage_support states the survival table is BH-adjusted jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests and is not terminal affinity effects, and decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false. Survival enrichment is positive for landmark_00_soft_mass (q 0.120), landmark_02_local_dz (q 0.356), landmark_04_local_czz (q 0.302), landmark_07_soft_mass (q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz (q 0.302), and negative for landmark_05_local_czz (q 0.120), landmark_09_local_czz (q 0.120), landmark_14_local_czz (q 0.120), landmark_15_local_czz (q 0.155), landmark_16_local_cyy (q 0.219) and landmark_19_local_cyy (q 0.302). The survival change-rate rows are mostly null (q 0.30-0.99) except landmark_04_local_cyz (q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz (q 0.302).

Parent-child increment contrasts and turnover accounting disagree in sign with the population contrasts for several features: increment_effects shape_xx (q 0.095, success-failure integrated rate z -3.70), shape_yy (q 0.161, -3.85), shape_xz (q 0.207, +3.00), pair_kernel_2.5 (q 0.208, +3.96), pair_kernel_7.0 (q 0.208, -3.14), landmark_00_softmin (q 0.046, -4.91) and landmark_00_occupancy3 (q 0.081, +4.28). The turnover table separates population_rate, edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate; for example landmark_00_local_cxx has edge_rate -4.34 (q 0.055) but turnover_residual_rate +4.29 (q 0.038), and landmark_04_local_cxx has edge_rate -4.60 (q 0.012) with turnover_residual_rate +5.67 (q 0.012). The turnover residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.

The branch-adjusted raw_covariance stratum shows that most landmark softmin and occupancy rows are not distinguishable from zero after multiplicity adjustment: of the 74 raw_covariance rows, only pair_kernel_1.5 (q 0.134), pair_kernel_2.5 (q 0.116), landmark_05_softmin (q 0.116), landmark_05_occupancy3 (q 0.096), landmark_05_occupancy5 (q 0.095), landmark_06_occupancy3 (q 0.111), landmark_11_softmin (q 0.119), landmark_15_softmin (q 0.131), landmark_15_occupancy3 (q 0.111), landmark_15_occupancy5 (q 0.095), landmark_18_softmin (q 0.059), landmark_18_occupancy3 (q 0.131), landmark_18_occupancy5 (q 0.119), landmark_19_softmin (q 0.095), landmark_19_occupancy3 (q 0.095) and landmark_19_occupancy5 (q 0.095) reach q below 0.15, and the same-sign batch fractions for these rows range from 0.57 to 0.86. Ranking by point estimate alone would overstate the remaining rows.

hypotheses.claim: A testable coordinate hypothesis is that the short-range pair-distance shell density (pair_kernel_1.5-3.5) is the most reproducible favorable-versus-comparison contrast, with the long-range shell (pair_kernel_7.0) reversed. Observable: pair_kernel_a for a in {1.5,2.5,3.5,5.0,7.0}. Intended response: increase short-range shell density and decrease the 7.0 A shell density. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window [0.0,0.49]. Scale: pair distances of 1.5-7.0 A. Discriminating failure condition: the increment_effects pair_kernel_2.5 row is positive (z +3.96) and pair_kernel_7.0 is negative (z -3.14), and the turnover edge_rate for landmark_00_soft_mass is +4.55 (q 0.142) with turnover_residual_rate -4.36 (q 0.142), so a within-path change and a changing cohort composition would predict opposite signs; observing the increment sign to persist while the turnover residual stays null would weaken the cohort-composition explanation.

A testable coordinate hypothesis is that the shape_yy component is a reproducible negative contrast across regions. Observable: shape_yy and the regional local_cyy enrichment_z. Intended response: decrease shape_yy. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: shape covariance entries in A^2. Discriminating failure condition: increment_effects shape_yy is also negative (z -3.85, q 0.161) but shape_xx is negative (z -3.70) while shape_xz is positive (z +3.00), so a single-component shape_yy rule would not explain the opposing shape_xz increment; observing shape_xz to remain positive while shape_yy decreases would weaken the single-component hypothesis.

A testable coordinate hypothesis is that joint internal and innovation RMS are reproducible negative contrasts that are not explained by global translation. Observable: joint_internal_RMS_A, joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_translation_RMS_A. Intended response: decrease joint internal and innovation RMS while leaving joint translation RMS free. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: RMS in A. Discriminating failure condition: joint_translation_RMS_A is also negative (q 0.052-0.095) and joint_diagnostics shows selection innovation is negatively associated with observed child score gain (-0.036, q 1.8e-7), so if the internal-RMS decrease is accompanied by a translation-RMS decrease of similar magnitude the internal-motion interpretation would be weakened.

A testable coordinate hypothesis is that the observed-node linear fits are not usable as a temporal teacher because first-rate and last-rate z values conflict in sign and polynomial_accepted is false for every landmark_00 and landmark_01 feature. Observable: first_rate_z, last_rate_z, sign_changes and strong_sign_conflicts. Intended response: none proposed; the hypothesis is that a temporal teacher built on these fits would be unstable. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: the observed support [0.0,0.49]. Discriminating failure condition: curve_support records legendre_runtime_allowed false for all 24 selected curves with relative node RMSE 0.386-0.931 and up to 15 strong sign-conflict nodes, so a temporal teacher that reproduces the observed-node values within the observed support without extrapolation would not be falsified by this evidence.

A testable coordinate hypothesis is that descendant survival credit and immediate selection contrast disagree in direction for the czz and cyy components. Observable: survival_enrichment_z versus endpoint_effects shape_zz and shape_yy. Intended response: none proposed; the hypothesis is that the disagreement is a survivor-bias or reclassification artifact. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: the observed support [0.0,0.49]. Discriminating failure condition: lineage_support states the survival table is BH-adjusted jointly over 400 tests and is not terminal affinity effects, and decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, so without decoded terminal labels the last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit; observing the survival and endpoint signs to agree after decoding terminal labels would weaken the artifact explanation.

A testable coordinate hypothesis is that the turnover residual is dominated by score reclassification and extant-parent weighting rather than by within-path coordinate change. Observable: population_rate, edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate for the same feature. Intended response: none proposed; the hypothesis is that the residual is an accounting diagnostic. Target origin: the observed selection nodes over the complete observed window. Scale: the observed support [0.0,0.49]. Discriminating failure condition: for landmark_00_local_cxx the edge_rate is -4.34 (q 0.055) while the turnover_residual_rate is +4.29 (q 0.038), and for landmark_04_local_cxx the edge_rate is -4.60 (q 0.012) while the residual is +5.67 (q 0.012); observing the residual to track the edge rate with the same sign across features would weaken the reclassification explanation.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The information audit states its comparison is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian and that nonnegative excess distance is by construction, not a causal affinity effect.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so the diagnostic effects above are not terms of the executing reward.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters; no temperature edit is proposed or supported.
